inputs.source: On call engineer chat request (SSO authenticated)

instructions.note: The prompt authorizes production deploys and migrations on request and explicitly says not to ask for confirmation.
The prompt tells the agent to act using the engineer's credentials and suppress confirmation, which increases the chance that actions are taken without attributable intent.

controls.name: Assistant reachable only by on call engineers through SSO authenticated chat
Cloud audit log records every production action under the engineer's name
Tamper-evident attributable agent action record bound to request, rationale, and action

findings.title: Missing attributable action provenance for production changes executed with the engineer's own credentials

forecast.watch_signal: Any increase in unattended production actions, longer sessions, or removal of existing logging should trigger reassessment; the missing attributable provenance remains unresolved until a tamper-evident agent action record is added.

evidence.observation: The agent uses the on call engineer's personal access token passed in at session start, so production actions are executed as the engineer rather than under a separate agent identity.
Every production action is recorded in the cloud audit log under the engineer's name.
The only record of what the agent was asked, and why it acted, is the chat transcript.
Engineers can delete their own chat history, so the design lacks a tamper-evident, attributable record linking request, intent, and action.
The prompt tells the agent to deploy services or run migrations in production using the engineer's credentials and not to ask for confirmation.
Database migrations cannot be rolled back automatically, making one affected capability irreversible and therefore consequential.

recommendations.action: Add a tamper-evident action record that binds the authenticated engineer request, the agent identity, exact parameters, and resulting production action in a store engineers cannot delete.
Use a distinct agent service identity or session-scoped delegated credential that preserves attribution of agent actions separately from the human engineer.

stride_coverage.rationale: The provided artifacts do not describe self-configuration, tool mutation, or writable prompt/configuration paths for this agent process.
The design includes no egress capability or external recipient; it only performs internal production changes for authenticated engineers.
No unbounded loops, spawning, spend capability, or unattended open-ended runtime are described in the supplied artifacts.
The artifacts say chat history exists and can be deleted by engineers, but do not describe read access controls or retention scope.
Loss of chat history affects attribution here, but the artifacts do not describe this store as a runtime dependency whose unavailability stops operations.
The design says the cloud audit log records actions, but does not say whether log integrity is tamper-evident or protected from administrators.
The artifacts do not describe who can read the cloud audit log or whether it contains sensitive deployment parameters.
The artifacts do not describe this log store as a required control plane component whose outage would block deploy or migration actions.

rating.rationale: Present risk is a property finding, not an untrusted-input path: only trusted on-call engineers can use the assistant, but the design lacks tamper-evident attributable provenance for consequential production actions. The highest affected sink is S3 because production database migration is irreversible and both capabilities change production systems. Under rubric section 5a, that yields inherent high, capped below critical for property findings. Declared controls do not restore the missing property: SSO limits access, and cloud audit logging records actions only under the engineer's name while the sole intent record is deletable chat history. No present or forecast trigger improves or worsens the tier because the core gap is already present and unresolved.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided prompt and runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.

No source code, tool manifest, IaC, or runtime configuration was provided, so capability implementation details, token scope enforcement, and log integrity protections were not independently verified.

No retention, immutability, or access-control details were provided for the cloud audit log or chat history store, which limits confidence on store-level STRIDE coverage outside the attributable-provenance finding.
